chapter: Chris Kelly and the country bands
title: Deer Range plantation brass band and its repertoire
summary: He mentions having his own band, then describes growing up at Deer Range, coming to New Orleans at 14 or 15; the country band played marches and quadrilles for dances and picnics, mostly not ragtime.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: his own band. That's what I heard. Yeah he had his own band one time. Just like me I had my own band one time. It was a name after me, Kit Stevenson. Oh yeah, Kit Stevenson. Yeah that's the time I was telling you about I and Sammy, Sammy Williams and Joy John always playing together at that time. Now you mentioned once was it Chris Kelly that taught me. That taught you down in the, that was on the plantation? No he taught me right here in New Orleans. He taught me in New Orleans. I wanted to go all the way back there to the plantation again. Did you live right at Deer Range? That's where I lived at Deer Range, plantation. Did you play in the brass band down there? I wanted to be sure to get all that. No I wasn't big enough. I wasn't old enough then. I was too small. When Jim Umpree was coming down there. Yeah I was a little bit of a fella. I was too small then. I just started playing when I came to New Orleans. I came to New Orleans when I was about 14 years old or 15 years old when I came to the city. Do you remember that band down there? How it sounded? What kind of a brass band it was? Oh they had a pretty good brass band. They had a pretty good brass band. Do you remember that they played for parades or dances? What did they do? Played for dances and parades. They played for, yeah they played for organizations. And they used to play on the art fellas parades. Because a lot of times my dad used to come here to the city. When they didn't have enough bands they used to send to the country and get bands. He used to come up here like on Labor Day. Yeah. In Conrad. They used to play up here on the parades at that time. Yeah. Oh it was wonderful in them days. Do you remember what kind of music they played? Was it all marches? Did they play any ragtime? No. Very few ragtime songs they used to play. Most of them were marches. Old time marches. Quadrilles and all.

Yeah and charters and all. You don't see that. With the brass band. With the brass band. The lanny waltzes do you remember? Yeah. All of that time. Yeah they used to play all that on that style. Not so much ragtime. No not too much ragtime.

I wondered. I wondered. Did they, the parades down there. Did they have much of a, was it a big enough town they put on many parades? Or what did they do down there? Well in that time they had plenty of people. Because it was a sugar farm. They used to raise sugar can. You see in that time. You used to have plenty of people out there. There were a lot of people there. Yeah. They used to go from different plantation you know. Like they give outnings and the band used to go to different places and give outnings. Play for different outnings. They have sort of picnics or what did they have? Picnics. Like that too. Uh huh. Even with Magnolia had a good band. Mr. Bear and Harrison Bonds used to play. Oh yeah. Sonny Henry and them fellas used to play. And another fella by the name of P.O. Anderson. He was a, he used to be a trumpet player too and he got off trumpet and got on Suzy phone. P.O. Anderson.
